Open the hive on a warm, still day, from the back, and keep the visit
short — every minute the box is open the colony loses heat it spent the
morning making.

Look for a solid brood pattern and a laying queen, not for every cell.
Queen cells hanging along the bottom edge of the comb mean swarming is
imminent; the same cells built across the face usually mean the colony
is replacing an old queen on its own. Two answers, opposite actions,
and the position of the cell is the whole of the difference.

Then count mites. An alcohol wash gives a number you can act on; a
glance at the bees gives a guess, and a guess is how a strong colony
is dead by autumn.
